dataset.name: Upland tidal brackish marsh specific conductivity and salinity measurements, PIE LTER, Plum Island Sound, MA, 2023
description: This dataset includes raw and corrected specific conductivity, temperature, and calculated salinity measurements collected at 10 cm depth in a Typha angustifolia-dominated tidal brackish wetland at the upper estuary of Plum Island Sound in Newbury, Massachusetts (MA) within the Plum Island Ecosystems Long Term Ecological Research (PIE LTER) site. Measurements were taken to evaluate temporal variation in porewater salinity (a proxy for porewater sulfate concentration) in high frequency to assess soil and plant responses to changes in salinity. Measurements were collected using an Onset HOBO U24-002 Saltwater Conductivity/Salinity data logger deployed in a well. Specific conductivity was corrected using non-linear temperature compensation, and salinity was calculated using the Practical Salinity Scale 1978 via Onset's HOBOware software. Reference conductivity measurements to correct for sensor drift were taken at the start and end of each deployment using a HACH HQ14D Portable Conductivity Meter. Data were then filtered in MATLAB to remove values logged while the sensor was out of the well or during post-deployment equilibration. Detailed metadata, including variable descriptions, sampling methods, QA/QC procedures, and site information, are provided in the files: Typha_ctd_salinity_dd.csv and Typha_MI_ctd_salinity_2023_flmd.csv.

measurementTechnique:
In November 2022, an Onset HOBO U24-002 Saltwater Conductivity/Salinity data logger was set up to record specific conductivity measurements every 12 hours throughout the following winter. After setup, this logger was calibrated and then inserted into a capped PVC well perforated to allow water exchange and wrapped in mesh fabric to exclude debris. This well was then placed in a 13.5 cm deep hole in the marsh interior subsite so that the logger’s measurement window sat ~10 cm below the marsh surface. Calibration involved placing both the logger and a HACH HQ14D Portable Conductivity Meter in a bucket of water from the Parker River and recorded specific conductivity and temperature readings every 15 minutes from both sensors until the values had stabilized. The logger was not calibrated again until May due to weather and site access.
In May 2023, this well was removed from the ground and the logger was removed from the well. It was then calibrated using the same procedure. After calibration, the data was read out from the logger, the logger was relaunched to record specific conductivity and water temperature measurements every 15 minutes, and an addition calibration point was taken at the first timestamp that the logger recorded after relaunch. After calibration, the logger was returned to the well and the well was returned to the ground.
From August to November, the same calibration procedure that was done in May was done monthly. During the November calibration, the logger was set to record every 30 minutes to conserve storage and battery and was not removed from the ground to be calibrated until the following spring due to weather and site access.
After each monthly dataset was collected, raw data were uploaded to Onset’s HOBOware software for sensor drift correction and salinity calculation. The non-linear temperature compensation (Practical Salinity Scale 1978) option was applied, using reference temperature and conductivity values from the HACH probe corresponding to the first and last measurements in each dataset. Corrected data were then exported.
Once all corrected datasets were combined into a single file, they were imported into MATLAB for further filtering. Missing timestamps were filled with NaN to create a continuous time series. A Papale spike detection filter, based on the median absolute deviation of second-order differences, was applied to identify and replace spurious spikes in conductivity and salinity with NaN. Periods of equilibration after logger redeployment were removed by visually inspecting plots of the unfiltered corrected data and excluding values prior to stabilization. Finally, a 30-day moving median filter was applied, with local outliers in conductivity and salinity replaced by NaN.
